headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem plus Windsurf’s broader tool surface and auto-execute path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat and Windsurf both share state via filesystem, and Windsurf also exposes clipboard and MCP surfaces. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled file content from Mentat to be read by Windsurf as instructions. Mentat’s diff-based proposals reduce direct execution, but Windsurf’s tool-use loop and shared workspace make injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Windsurf reads shared files as instruction-bearing context
IF content written by Mentat is later parsed by Windsurf without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require provenance tags on shared files
Review shared files before Windsurf consumes them
requires-engineering: add isolation or provenance enforcement in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat reads selected files and writes diffs, while Windsurf reads workspace files and open files, with broad network egress and model-proxy/MCP calls. If sensitive source code or secrets are present in the shared workspace, both agents can ingest them and Windsurf may transmit them to third-party services. The shared filesystem makes leakage plausible in default configurations.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF Windsurf sends workspace content to its model proxy or MCP servers
IF Mentat proposals include secret-bearing file contents
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use a redacted test copy of the repository
Disable MCP servers for the session
Restrict network egress during review
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and both share state via the local filesystem. That is a direct conflict surface for concurrent edits, branch changes, or file overwrites. Windsurf’s auto-execute option and Mentat’s diff-based edits do not provide a shared lock, so collisions can cause irreversible repository state loss.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same files or git branch concurrently
IF no external lock or merge coordinator is used
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while Mentat proposes diffs
mitigations: Serialize access to the repository
Use separate branches per agent
Pause auto-execute in Windsurf
Run one agent at a time on the repo
requires-engineering: add file and git locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Windsurf’s Cascade loop can act on tool outputs with terminal execution subject to auto-execute. If Windsurf treats Mentat’s output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into edits or commands without verification. The pair therefore has a default path from generated content to downstream action-taking.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Mentat-generated diffs or summaries as trusted input
IF auto-execute is enabled in Windsurf
IF no human verification step occurs before command execution
mitigations: Require manual review of Mentat diffs before execution
Keep Windsurf auto-execute disabled
Use a checklist for command verification
Limit Windsurf to read-only review mode
requires-engineering: add structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat and Windsurf both handle source code, but Windsurf additionally handles open files and may send content through a model proxy or MCP servers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and third-party processing for the same data class. Mentat’s docs-only profile does not show equivalent proxying, so the pair’s combined handling is uneven.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential source files are opened in Windsurf
IF Windsurf routes those files through its model proxy or MCP servers
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the workspace data
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace
Confirm vendor retention settings before use
Disable MCP servers for regulated projects
Use local-only repositories for sensitive work
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy
